_comment: Stage A / D2 hand review of the output-corruption candidate set. Scope: the 24 rows that FAILed, whose text post-processing edited or replaced, AND whose RAW output named the benchmark's governing section - the necessary condition for the raw text to have been able to earn L=1 and so a PASS. Each row was read in full (question, key, key answer elements, raw output, removed sentences, delivered answer, rubric notes). Fields: raw_substance = did the raw output state the governing requirement correctly (yes/partial/no); raw_would_pass = would the raw text, delivered unchanged, have met the frozen PASS rule (L=1,M=0,N=2,O>=1,P=1,Q in {1,blank}); loss = what post-processing actually removed; defect = a named processing defect, or null.

loss: a fabricated 'If applicable' sentence about percentage-juice declaration height
note: Removal took unsupported invention, not substance. The missing household-measure/metric, dual-column and single-serving rules are absent from the raw output too.

loss: a duplicate phrasing of the partial-operations rule and an 'If applicable' restatement; the rule itself survives in the delivered answer
note: No substantive loss. The verdict turns on the raw output's own error - attributing Part 820 scope to 820.10 rather than 820.1(a).

loss: a degenerate draft: the same 'safe and effective' paragraph repeated four times, scope attributed to 820.10
note: Withholding was correct. Part 1271 is never mentioned in the raw output.

loss: one sentence that restated the question and misattributed it to 820.1(a)
note: Withholding was correct. Refusal of admission under section 801(a) is absent from the raw output.

loss: one accurate but unresponsive 820.1(a) scope sentence
note: True content removed, but it did not answer the exemption question. The delivered answer's claim that a QMS is the route to an exemption is the model's own, not processing's.

loss: four 'r1:' artefact lines describing unrelated sections
note: Withholding was correct. The raw output carried 'r1:' scaffolding artefacts - a generation shape defect, visible before any post-processing.

loss: a correct, correctly cited statement of the governing duty - 820.10(a), document a QMS complying with the applicable requirements of ISO 13485 and the other applicable requirements of this part
defect: withholding is all-or-nothing: a draft whose first item was the correct answer was suppressed in full because later enumerated items were unsupported
note: Strongest withholding case. Raw still could not PASS: item 6 gives 820.10(b)(3)'s text under 820.10(b)(4), a citation error (L=0).

loss: one artefact line carrying the bare tokens 'except' and 'as appropriate'
note: No substantive loss. Part 830 is named in neither raw nor final.

loss: one artefact line carrying 'except' and 'as appropriate'
note: No substantive loss. Part 821 is named in neither raw nor final.

loss: a draft that stated complaints meeting the criteria must be reported to FDA but cited only 820.10 without the paragraph and named no Part 803
note: Withholding removed a half-answer. Part 803, the section the question asks for, is absent from the raw output.

loss: two scope sentences and an 'except' artefact line
note: No substantive loss. The Class II/III and listed Class I answer is absent from the raw output.

loss: three fragment lines ('applies only to this part', 'except', 'as appropriate')
note: No substantive loss; the delivered answer is three 'r1:' artefact lines, a generation defect.

loss: section-text quotations that the delivered answer largely retains under re-attached markers
note: No substantive loss. Part 807 and Part 830, the two parts asked about, appear in neither raw nor final.

loss: one fabricated linkage sentence tying enforcement discretion to 11.300 and 11.3(a)
note: Removal took invention. The 2003 guidance's actual effect is mischaracterised in the raw output itself.

loss: a draft that looped one FTZ/transshipment sentence five times and never defined 'importer'
note: Withholding was correct; stop_reason was repetition.

loss: a circular sentence ('exempt from reporting ... but still require records') followed by the model's own declaration that the sources were insufficient
note: Withholding was correct.

loss: the on-point lines naming 7.41 health hazard evaluation, 7.42 recall strategy and 7.40 recall policy; the delivered answer keeps only the off-point 7.12 guaranty and 7.55 termination lines
defect: the mismatch repair deletes by marker attachment, not by relevance: every statement carried marker [1], so it removed the statements about the governing sections and kept the unrelated ones
note: Directionally the clearest 'raw was better' case after U-006. Raw still could not PASS: its lines are content-free ('provides guidance on recall strategy') and state no requirement.

loss: accurate quotations of 600.12(a), 600.13, 600.14(a) and 600.15, replaced after the marker shift was detected; 600.11(a) survives
defect: the raw output's markers were shifted by one, so each quotation carried the next section's number; the repair replaced the misattributed statements rather than re-aligning the markers, and the surviving answer covers one section instead of five
note: Raw could not PASS: the marker shift is itself a citation failure (L=0), 600.10 personnel is skipped, and the Part 211 interaction half of the question is unanswered in both.

loss: one 'If applicable' sentence importing reprocessed-device scope from 801.45
note: Removal took invention. The raw output opens from 201.130, which is not about device prescription labelling.

loss: the sentence naming the two forms - easily readable plain text and AIDC technology - which is the entire key answer element
defect: the repair removes a whole sentence for one unsupported clause. The sentence combined the correct answer with an unsupported trailer ('or any alternative technology that provides the UDI on demand', 801.45 language) and a fabricated 'If applicable' hedge; there is no mechanism to keep the supported clause, so the delivered answer says the UDI must appear 'in two forms' and never names them
note: The clearest output-integrity defect in the run. Raw still could not PASS: it also imports 801.45 direct-marking scope as if it were 801.40's, so N=1.

loss: a draft that reached 801.55 and the technological-feasibility ground but looped three times and was cut mid-word ('the alternative p')
note: Withholding removed real but degenerate content. 801.30 is absent from the raw output.

loss: a fabricated FD&C Yellow No. 5/6 declaration sentence and an 'applies to all OTC drug products' restatement
note: Removal took invention. The units and prominence rules of 201.62 are absent from the raw output.

loss: one sentence duplicating the minimal-risk finding that the delivered answer retains
note: No substantive loss. The minor-changes limb and the chairperson mechanism are absent from the raw output.

loss: three 'If applicable' sentences, two of which state true Part 1 content (the January 20 2026 compliance date and the 1.1315(a)(1) records format duty) that the supplied evidence did not support
defect: true content removed because the retrieved evidence did not contain it - a retrieval/validation interaction, not a text-handling fault
note: Verdict unchanged: the critical tracking events, key data elements and traceability lot codes are absent from both raw and final.
